title: Historic Town of Zabid
supports: Historic urban plan, mosque concentration, domestic architecture and endangered World Heritage status.
hidden_gem_rationale: Zabid's dense network of simple brick mosques and Tihama courtyard houses creates a coherent urban-architecture study distinct from Yemen's highland tower cities.

title: The Trails
supports: Niha trail network, reserve context, difficulty choices and trail-use planning.
hidden_gem_rationale: A quieter southern reserve entrance links varied trail difficulty with a different sector of the biosphere reserve rather than repeating the best-known cedar stand.

title: Plan Your Visit
supports: Reserve trails, cedar-clad cliffs, visitor rules and advance planning.
hidden_gem_rationale: Steep cliff-hanging cedar habitat and official trail rules make this a protected-landscape walk distinct from a roadside visit to Lebanon's headline grove.

title: Gibran Kahlil Gibran Museum
supports: Museum in the former Mar Sarkis monastery and holdings of manuscripts, artworks and personal objects.
hidden_gem_rationale: The combination of a former hermitage with Gibran's studio furniture, manuscripts and hundreds of artworks supports a focused author-artist archive visit.

title: The Building
supports: Birzeit museum's terraced landscape, gardens and relationship between architecture, land and native planting.
hidden_gem_rationale: The designed terraces interpret native and naturalised plants as cultural and agricultural history, making the landscape an experience unit beyond the indoor museum.

title: Ancient City of Bosra
supports: Nabataean, Roman, Byzantine and Islamic layers, caravan-route role and major monuments.
hidden_gem_rationale: Bosra's preserved Roman theatre, early Christian ruins and mosques can be read together as successive layers of one caravan city rather than as isolated monuments.

title: Ashur (Qal'at Sherqat)
supports: Assyria's first capital, religious importance, Tigris setting and World Heritage status.
hidden_gem_rationale: Temples, three ziggurats, palaces and domestic quarters together reveal how Assyria's religious capital developed before the later imperial capitals.

title: The Ahwar of Southern Iraq: Refuge of Biodiversity and the Relict Landscape of the Mesopotamian Cities
supports: Four marshland components, three archaeological cities and combined natural-cultural significance.
hidden_gem_rationale: The serial property uniquely connects four wetland ecosystems with the archaeological landscapes of Uruk, Ur and Eridu in one combined cultural-natural framework.

title: Cultural Landscape of Maymand
supports: Seasonal pastoral system, hand-carved dwellings and living cultural landscape.
hidden_gem_rationale: The continuing three-season pastoral movement gives the hand-carved winter dwellings meaning as one component of a living land-use system.

title: Hyrcanian Forests
supports: Serial ancient broad-leaved forest property, exceptional biodiversity and protected components in Iran.
hidden_gem_rationale: A carefully selected authorised component would interpret a relict broad-leaved forest ecosystem and endemic biodiversity rather than offer a generic woodland walk.

title: Shushtar Historical Hydraulic System
supports: Interconnected canals, tunnels, mills, dams and bridges forming an ancient water-management system.
hidden_gem_rationale: Following the linked canals, tunnels, dams, bridges and mills reveals a city-scale engineered system rather than a single landmark.
